new_public_evidence.source: Liu, Wu, Summa & Zheng, Adaptive Multilevel Twisted Sequential Monte Carlo for Rare Events Estimation in Language Models
new_public_evidence.result: Very recent arXiv v1 directly applies progressive multilevel rare-event proposal learning to LLM unsafe-behavior estimation. Ideal analysis changes positive-sample dependence from Theta(1/p*) to polylogarithmic in 1/p*; imperfect-proposal theorem retains the advantage when TV error stays below the per-level retained fraction. Toxic-story and StrongREJECT experiments show large reductions in zero-hit/large-error failures at comparable training runtime in tested settings.

new_public_evidence.source: Budde et al., Analysis of non-Markovian repairable fault trees through rare event simulation
new_public_evidence.result: Formal-methods/system-reliability importance-splitting study gives a closer non-finance analogue: a best case has about 100x narrower CI than crude MC at fixed runtime, while mismatched thresholds or a time-insensitive importance function cause oversampling, resets and null estimates in other cases.

new_public_evidence.source: Peherstorfer, Willcox & Gunzburger, Optimal Model Management for Multifidelity Monte Carlo Estimation
new_public_evidence.result: Arbitrary surrogate collections can be optimally sampled with occasional high-fidelity recourse, preserving an unbiased estimator of the high-fidelity statistic even without surrogate error bounds; numerical experiments report orders-of-magnitude speedups in tested linear/nonlinear problems.

derived_results.claim: r104's adaptive rare-event ladder now has direct LLM-safety evidence. The central mechanism is not merely trajectory cloning: maintain a sequence of nested score events so each learned proposal supplies enough importance-corrected positives to train the next rarer proposal. In the ideal theorem this converts positive-example acquisition from inverse rare-event probability to polylogarithmic dependence; the practical experiments show that standard Twisted SMC can collapse to zero hits while multilevel training retains useful hit rate/ESS.

Across fault-tree splitting and LLM twisted SMC, score/reaction-coordinate quality is a first-class bottleneck. It controls level geometry and proposal quality; importance weighting corrects proposal mismatch but does not repair semantic misclassification of the target event. Any adaptation must log score error/coverage, level-transition hit rates, ESS/weight degeneracy and reset/oversampling events separately.

For non-rare continuous/average metrics, a safer proxy-use pattern is multifidelity control/model management with explicit high-fidelity correction. This keeps the target estimator unbiased under the cited MFMC construction even when surrogate error bounds are absent, rather than treating a proxy score as target truth.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The LLM paper is a new arXiv v1 preprint dated 2026-08-22; its theory uses ideal or bounded-TV-error proposal assumptions and does not prove end-to-end learned-runtime polylogarithmic complexity.
The paper's estimator targets the practical score-defined rare event unless score error is separately bounded; proposal importance correction cannot make an imperfect evaluator semantically correct.
The fault-tree approximately-100x CI result is a case-specific best result and the same study documents serious splitting failures under mismatched dynamics/thresholds.
Multifidelity orders-of-magnitude speedups require useful surrogate correlations/cost ratios; unbiasedness does not guarantee variance reduction.
No AGI capability conclusion follows. These are evaluation-budget mechanisms.

candidate_update.rare_event: strengthened: direct LLM-safety + formal system-reliability evidence, with score-quality and estimator-correction guardrails
candidate_update.multifidelity: strengthened: arbitrary-surrogate optimal model management with explicit high-fidelity unbiased correction
